# vendor/ob3

- `ob_v3p0_achievementcredential_schema.json` — official Open Badges 3.0 `AchievementCredential` JSON Schema, fetched from `https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/ob/v3p0/schema/json/ob_v3p0_achievementcredential_schema.json` on 2026-08-19. Vendored so schema validation (tests/CI) never depends on network access at runtime.
- `credentials-v2.jsonld` — the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 `@context`, fetched from `https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2` (with `Accept: application/ld+json`) on 2026-08-19.
- `ob-context-3.0.3.jsonld` — the Open Badges 3.0 `@context`, fetched from `https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/ob/v3p0/context-3.0.3.json` on 2026-08-19.

Both are served from disk by `app/lib/document-loader.js`, which is the only JSON-LD documentLoader wired into signing/verification (see Task 7) — it never falls back to a network-fetching loader, so any URL it doesn't recognize is a hard error.

**DID/security contexts were investigated but NOT vendored.** The local issuer DID document (`app/lib/issuer-key.js#getDidDocument()`) declares `@context: ["https://www.w3.org/ns/did/v1", "https://w3id.org/security/multikey/v1"]`. We suspected proof verification might need to dereference those contexts too, so we ran a real `@digitalbazaar/vc` `issue()`/`verifyCredential()` round trip (Ed25519/eddsa-rdfc-2022 Data Integrity proof) through a logging documentLoader and observed every URL actually requested. Neither context URL was ever requested during verification, for two SEPARATE reasons — one per resolved URL:

1. `ISSUER_DID#key-0` (the verificationMethod URL from the proof) resolves to the verificationMethod object itself (not the full did document — see the loader's own header comment for why that distinction matters). `@digitalbazaar/data-integrity`'s `getVerificationMethod()` and `@digitalbazaar/ed25519-multikey`'s `from()` consume that object directly, with no jsonld expansion of its own `@context`; the Multikey context match inside `ed25519-multikey` is a plain string-equality check, not a fetch.
2. The bare `ISSUER_DID` (the controller document, checked by `AssertionProofPurpose`/`ControllerProofPurpose` against `assertionMethod`) resolves to the full did document, and jsonld-signatures' `ControllerProofPurpose#validate()` has a `mustFrame` optimization (`node_modules/jsonld-signatures/lib/purposes/ControllerProofPurpose.js`) that **skips `jsonld.frame()` entirely** — and therefore never dereferences the document's own `@context` — when the checked term is a DID verification-relationship term (`assertionMethod` is one) AND the document's `@context` is exactly `https://www.w3.org/ns/did/v1` or an array whose **first element** is that URL. `getDidDocument()` puts `did/v1` first, so this optimization always fires today.

**Invariant this loader's network-freedom depends on:** `issuer-key.js#getDidDocument()` must keep `https://www.w3.org/ns/did/v1` as the first element of its `@context` array (see the comment on that array in `app/lib/issuer-key.js`). We proved the dependency by reproduction: reordering that array (`multikey/v1` first) makes `ControllerProofPurpose` run `jsonld.frame()`, which then requests `https://w3id.org/security/multikey/v1` through the pinned loader and fails verification (rejected, since it isn't vendored — error surfaced by jsonld as "Dereferencing a URL did not result in a valid JSON-LD object"). If that document's `@context` shape ever changes, either restore did/v1-first, or vendor both DID/security contexts here and stop rejecting them.

Both resolved URLs (`ISSUER_DID` and `ISSUER_DID#key-0`) are served locally via `app/lib/issuer-key.js`, not vendored files. Per "vendor only what's actually needed", `https://www.w3.org/ns/did/v1` and `https://w3id.org/security/multikey/v1` are therefore rejected by the pinned loader like any other unpinned URL; see `test/document-loader.test.js` and `task-6-report.md` for the evidence.
